record.paper_title: Cooperative Games with Incomplete Information: Some Open Problems
record.original_question: Beyond the currently known positive results for quasilinear economies and other special assumptions, what alternative economically interesting assumptions or scenarios guarantee non-emptiness of interim core concepts for exchange economies with asymmetric information, including cores defined through equilibrium blocking or related mechanism-based objections?

evidence.quote: Understanding the limitations that these and other conditions may have, the search for alternative interesting scenarios in which non-emptiness of the core obtains should also be part of the research agenda.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a pure exchange economy with asymmetric information specified as follows. There is a finite set N = {1, ..., n} of agents and a finite set Ω of states of nature with a common prior probability μ on Ω. The commodity space is R^ℓ_+ for some ℓ ≥ 1. Each agent i ∈ N is endowed with:
(i) a measurable state-contingent initial endowment e_i : Ω → R^ℓ_+;
(ii) a private information partition F_i of Ω (so that agent i, at the interim stage, knows only the element F_i(ω) ∈ F_i containing the realized state ω);
(iii) a state-dependent utility function u_i : R^ℓ_+ × Ω → R, with interim expected utility
   V_i(x_i | F_i(ω)) = Σ_{ω' ∈ F_i(ω)} μ(ω' | F_i(ω)) u_i(x_i(ω'), ω')
for any feasible state-contingent consumption plan x_i : Ω → R^ℓ_+.

A feasible allocation is a profile (x_i)_{i ∈ N} with Σ_i x_i(ω) ≤ Σ_i e_i(ω) for every ω ∈ Ω. Given a notion of "blocking" by a coalition S ⊆ N at the interim stage — which may be defined via (a) direct interim improvement using pooled or private information, (b) credible/incentive-compatible objections, or (c) equilibrium-based blocking through a mechanism implementable within S — one obtains a corresponding interim core: the set of feasible allocations against which no coalition has a valid objection.

Beyond the case of quasilinear utilities (where u_i(x_i, ω) is linear in some numeraire commodity) and a small list of other special structural assumptions known to ensure non-emptiness, identify and rigorously establish further economically meaningful classes of assumptions on the data (Ω, μ, (e_i, F_i, u_i)_{i ∈ N}) under which the interim core — in particular cores defined through equilibrium blocking or mechanism-based objections — is guaranteed to be non-empty.
artifact.status_search_result: The literature provides non-emptiness results for specific interim core concepts under restrictive assumptions (e.g., quasilinearity/sidepayments, balanced structures, independent types, incentive-compatible coarse core), while the Bayesian incentive-compatible interim core can be empty (Hahn–Yannelis 1997). A general characterization of economically interesting conditions ensuring non-emptiness of interim cores — especially those defined via equilibrium or mechanism-based blocking — has not been established, and the search for such conditions is identified as an ongoing research agenda.

status_evidence.title: Interim core concepts for a Bayesian pure exchange economy
status_evidence.snippet: Sufficient conditions for nonemptiness of the Bayesian incentive-compatible interim core are formulated; without them, the core may be empty.
status_evidence.claim: Non-emptiness of the interim core is known only under specific sufficient conditions; the general problem remains open.

status_evidence.title: Incentives and the core of an exchange economy: a survey
status_evidence.snippet: Survey discusses positive and negative results on non-emptiness for various core notions under asymmetric information.
status_evidence.claim: The literature shows fragmentary positive results, motivating the search for additional scenarios.

status_evidence.title: Incomplete Information, Credibility and the Core (Dutta–Vohra)
status_evidence.snippet: Develops credible/mechanism-based core notions for economies with incomplete information.
status_evidence.claim: Mechanism-based interim cores are an active area without general non-emptiness theorems.
